entities.summary: Juan de Jaso (b. 1445, Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port) was a navigator of the Medieval period, shaped by feudalism, religious institutions, and cultural exchange, active in Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port. He played a key role in the establishment of trade routes between Europe and the Mediterranean, contributing to the growth of the city's mercantile economy. De Jaso's navigation skills and knowledge of the region helped to facilitate the exchange of goods, ideas, and cultures between the Catholic Church and the Ottoman Empire. His legacy can be seen in the development of maritime trade routes that connected Europe to the Middle East and Africa. The establishment of the Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port navigation school, which he co-founded, served as a model for maritime education in the region. De Jaso's contributions to the field of navigation were recognized by his peers, who praised his expertise in charting the coastlines of the Atlantic Ocean. As a result of his work, the city of Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port became an important hub for maritime trade and commerce, solidifying its position as a major center of economic activity in the region. The legacy of Juan de Jaso can still be seen in the modern-day shipping lanes that connect Europe to the Mediterranean and the Middle East, a testament to his enduring impact on the development of maritime trade.
